title: Inviting a teammate throws ‘object is not extensible’
why: The error names property '2' on an object you never wrote. The actual cause is a push onto frozen Redux state, several layers away.
finding: `projectMembers/invite` rejected with `TypeError: Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible`. The members list stayed at 2 and the email stayed in the input.
actual: The invite thunk throws a TypeError 'Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible' (projectMembers/invite/rejected). No member is added — the list still shows only dev@example.local (Owner) and collaborator@example.com (Member), and newmember@example.com remains in the input field.
expected: Clicking Invite with a valid email should add the new member to the Team Members list as a 'Member' (e.g. newmember@example.com shown with a Member badge) and clear the input field.

chronology.text: On the Settings tab, in the Team Members section, the user has typed 'newmember@example.com' into the 'Enter email address to invite' field (which enabled the Invite button) and clicks the 'Invite' button — a \<button type="submit" class="settings-section__save-btn" data-testid="invite-btn" data-analytics-event="project-members-invite-submit">. The user expects this to add newmember@example.com to the Team Members list as a Member. _User interaction._

chronology.text: Immediately after the click, the invite fails: the Redux thunk projectMembers/invite is rejected with TypeError 'Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible'. The Team Members list is unchanged — it still shows only dev@example.local (Owner) and collaborator@example.com (Member); newmember@example.com was NOT added and remains in the invite input field. The user is left with an error and no new member.

reproduce.text: Scroll to the 'Team Members' section (current members: dev@example.local Owner, collaborator@example.com Member).
Type a valid email (e.g. newmember@example.com) into the 'Enter email address to invite' field — the Invite button becomes enabled.
Observe: an error 'Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible' appears and the member is not added to the list.

rootCause.text: In src/dev/mockPipeline.ts, mockInviteMember reads the project's member array with `const list = store.membersByProject[projectId] ?? []` and then calls `list.push(m)` (mockPipeline.ts:1365-1366). That array is the exact same object reference that was previously stored into Redux state at src/slices/projectMembersSlice.ts:106 (`state.items = action.payload.items`), because mockFetchProjectMembers returns `store.membersByProject[projectId]` directly (mockPipeline.ts:1349). Redux Toolkit (Immer) freezes state in development, so once that array was placed in the store it became non-extensible. Calling Array.push on the now-frozen array throws 'TypeError: Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible' (the existing array already holds 2 members at indices 0 and 1, so adding index 2 fails). The rejected projectMembers/invite action's error has name 'TypeError', message 'Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible', and a stack of 'at Array.push → at Module.mockInviteMember (mockPipeline.ts) → at handleInvite (ProjectMembers.tsx:39)'. The thunk rejects, no member is appended, and the member is never added.

rootCauseSteps.text: The thunk calls mockInviteMember, which runs `list.push(m)` on store.membersByProject[projectId] — the same array reference Immer froze when it became Redux state.items. Array.push on the frozen array throws 'TypeError: Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible', so the thunk dispatches projectMembers/invite/rejected and the member is never appended to the list.
